chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Samaan, who said:

I asked him about a slave whom his master manumits by installments (mukatabah), while the master knows that the slave has neither little nor much wealth. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He manumits him, even if the slave asks the people [for money], and his lack of wealth does not prevent the manumitation, for indeed Allah provides for the servants one from another, and the benefactor is assisted [by Allah].'

key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبَةَ: The contract of manumission by installments

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on mukatabah if the master knows the slave has no money?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies that a master's knowledge of the slave's poverty does not invalidate the mukatabah contract, emphasizing that financial capacity is not a strict prerequisite for eligibility. It highlights the theological principle that sustenance (rizq) is distributed among people, encouraging masters to facilitate manumission as an act of benevolence that invites divine aid. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic view that mukatabah is a right of the slave to seek freedom, rather than merely a commercial transaction dependent on immediate liquidity.
